Four independent implementations that deliberately track ISO 15118-3's Annex A parameter set — EVerest/libslac, SwitchEV/pyslac, the hupe1980/iso15118 Rust crate, and the DIN SPEC 70122 TTCN-3 conformance tests — each enumerate the same Table A.1 family (C_EV_match_MNBC, C_EV_match_retry, C_EV_start_atten_char_inds, TT_EVSE_SLAC_init, TT_EV_atten_results, TT_EVSE_match_MNBC, TT_match_sequence, TT_match_response, TT_EVSE_match_session, TT_match_join, T_step_EF, TP_EV_batch_msg_interval, TP_EV_vald_*). Not one of them contains a signal-strength or attenuation threshold parameter. Four independent omissions of a parameter that would sit between C_EV_match_retry and C_EV_start_atten_char_inds is meaningful negative evidence.

3. One independent source contradicts the premise directly. The hupe1980/iso15118 crate documents its optional attenuation limit as: "`None` accepts any run and leaves the choice entirely to the vehicle, which is what ISO 15118-3 describes." That asserts ISO 15118-3 specifies no normative dB threshold — the opposite of what a normatively-sourced C_EV_match_signalattn_indirect would imply.

4. Where an independent attenuation threshold does exist, it disagrees: 40, not 20, and it is a single threshold rather than a direct/indirect pair. Qualcomm's open-plc-utils defines SLAC_LIMIT 40 and exposes it as a user-settable "AttenuationThreshold" ini key; pyslac inherits the same 40. Both are stating their own implementation choice — pyslac annotates its genuinely normative constants with the ISO symbol and pointedly does not annotate SLAC_LIMIT. So this is a different kind of evidence, and it is not corroboration of 20 dB.

5. Two problems with the report itself, independent of corroboration:
   - Wrong lines. In model/timing.ceps, `label table_a_1_4` and `val C_EV_match_signalattn_indirect = 20.0;` are at lines 72-73. Lines 75-76 are `label table_a_1_5` / `val C_EV_start_atten_char_inds = 3;`. The value attribution is right, the line cite is off by three.
   - The unit is inferred, not stated. The file writes `val C_EV_match_signalattn_indirect = 20.0;` with no unit — timing entries in the same file carry an explicit `*s`, this one carries nothing. "20 dB" is the reporter's reading of "signal strength measurement", not the source's word. Reasonable given HPGP encodes attenuation in dB over 0-60 dB, but it should not be quoted as if the source said dB.
   - Additionally, the cepsdev repo asserts conformance to ISO 15118-3 in its README but the file carries no clause or table citation beyond its own `table_a_1_N` labels, so it is a single unverified transcription, not a chain back to the standard.

A targeted web search could still turn something up; I would not upgrade this to "the value is wrong", only to "the value is unsupported by anything I can reach".

RECOMMENDATION for the detector: do not cite C_EV_match_signalattn_indirect as a normative symbol. On present evidence ISO 15118-3 does not appear to fix a dB acceptance threshold for SLAC at all — the attenuation comparison is the EV's choice among the CM_ATTEN_CHAR.INDs it collects, which is why independent EVSE-side implementations either omit a threshold or make it an optional local policy. A fleet-measured threshold is the honest thing to keep here; the normative symbol you can legitimately cite for an unanswered CM_SLAC_MATCH.REQ is TT_match_response = 200 ms with C_EV_match_retry = 2 retries, bounded by TT_EVSE_match_session = 10 s — all four independent sources agree on those, and the 10 s in your current rule matches TT_EVSE_match_session exactly.

EVerest/libslac @ main carries a byte-identical constants block (include/slac/slac.hpp L43-55) — same upstream, so treat the two as one source, not two independent confirmations.
- qca/open-plc-utils @ master — slac/slac.h, slac/evse.ini, slac/pev.ini, slac/pev.c, slac/evse.c, slac/pev_cm_slac_match.c, slac/pev_cm_slac_param.c, slac/pev_cm_start_atten_char.c, slac/pev_cm_mnbc_sound.c, slac/evse_cm_mnbc_sound.c, slac/evse_cm_slac_param.c.

- uhi22/ccs32clara @ main — ccs/homeplug.cpp. This is a C++ port of pyPLC's SLAC FSM with the same numbers; it is a corroboration of pyPLC, not an independent data point.

WHICH SOURCES CARRY NORMATIVE WEIGHT
Only two of the four codebases name ISO 15118-3 symbols at all:
- pyslac is the strongest: `class Timers` docstring says "Timeouts defined by ISO15118-3 in table A.1", every member carries the ISO symbol in a trailing comment, and the file additionally quotes ISO requirement IDs verbatim — [V2G3-M06-05] … [V2G3-M06-09], [V2G2-852], [V2G2-853], [V2G2-931] (enums.py L3-L41) and [V2G3-A09-19], [V2G3-A09-30], [V2G3-A09-31], [V2G3-A09-47], [V2G3-A09-124], [V2G3-A09-125] (session.py). Those requirement IDs are the most citable thing I found: they are clause-level handles, not just symbol names.
- EVerest names the symbols but gives no clause or table: the whole block sits under `// FIXME (aw): where to put these iso15118/3 consts?`. Values agree with pyslac everywhere they overlap, which is what makes the shared ones high-confidence.
- open-plc-utils predates ISO 15118-3 framing entirely. Its comments reference HPGP ("we broadcast three times per HPGP specification") and it uses one generic 1000 ms socket read timeout for every exchange. Useful as evidence that a value is HomePlug GP heritage rather than ISO-invented, and nothing more.
- pyPLC/ccs32clara values are empirical, derived from sniffing a Hyundai Ioniq and testing against Alpitronic/ABB/Compleo/Tesla chargers; comments say so ("original from ioniq is ..."). Do not cite pyPLC for a normative number.

DIRECT ANSWER FOR THE DETECTOR RULE ("unanswered match request for 10 s")
The 10 s currently in the rule coincides numerically with TT_EVSE_match_session = 10 s, but that symbol means something different from what the rule measures, so which symbol to cite depends on how the rule is actually computed:
1. If the rule is "EV sent CM_SLAC_MATCH.REQ and no CM_SLAC_MATCH.CNF followed" — the normative symbol is TT_match_response = 200 ms, bounded by C_EV_match_retry = 2. EVerest implements exactly this: fsm/ev/src/states/others.cpp `MatchRequestState::send_match_req()` arms TT_MATCH_RESPONSE_MS after each CM_SLAC_MATCH.REQ and gives up once `num_of_tries >= C_EV_MATCH_RETRY`, so a conformant EV declares failure after about 3 × 200 ms ≈ 600 ms. The fleet-measured 10 s is ~50× that limit: safe as a detector threshold, but the citation should say the threshold is deliberately loose relative to TT_match_response rather than implying 10 s is the norm.
2. If the rule is really "the EVSE got CM_ATTEN_CHAR.RSP and CM_SLAC_MATCH.REQ never arrived" — then TT_EVSE_match_session = 10 s is the exact symbol, and the existing 10 s is normative as-is. EVerest arms precisely this at matching_handle_slac.cpp L356-359 on entering WAIT_FOR_SLAC_MATCH, and pyslac uses it as the read timeout in cm_slac_match() (session.py L706). This is the citation I would use if the detector's timer starts at CM_ATTEN_CHAR.RSP.
A packet-capture detector watching for a REQ with no matching CNF is doing (1); if it is instead watching for a sequence that stalls after CM_ATTEN_CHAR, it is doing (2). Worth checking the detector's trigger point before picking the symbol — the two differ by a factor of 50.

STATE MACHINE STRUCTURE (EVSE side, from EVerest — the most explicit FSM of the four)
Top-level states: Reset → Idle → Matching → (WaitForLink) → Matched, plus Failed. `MatchingState` holds a vector of per-EV `MatchingSession` objects keyed by (EV MAC, RunID), so one EVSE can track several EVs sounding at once; each session carries its own single-shot timeout (`next_timeout` / `timeout_active`) and its own `num_retries`. Sub-states and the timer armed on entry to each:
  WAIT_FOR_START_ATTEN_CHAR — TT_match_sequence (400 ms), armed after sending CM_SLAC_PARM.CNF
  SOUNDING — TT_EVSE_match_MNBC (600 ms), armed on CM_START_ATTEN_CHAR.IND
  FINALIZE_SOUNDING — 45 ms implementation grace delay
  WAIT_FOR_ATTEN_CHAR_RSP — TT_match_response (200 ms), armed after sending CM_ATTEN_CHAR.IND
  WAIT_FOR_SLAC_MATCH — TT_EVSE_match_session (10 s), armed on CM_ATTEN_CHAR.RSP
  RECEIVED_SLAC_MATCH → MATCH_COMPLETE (timeout set to 0, fires immediately)
  FAILED
Entry to MatchingState arms a separate `timeout_slac_parm_req` = slac_init_timeout_ms (TT_EVSE_SLAC_init) for the very first CM_SLAC_PARM.REQ. - EVerest EVSE has `reset_instead_of_fail` (manifest default true): on the first FAILED it clears all sessions, re-arms TT_EVSE_SLAC_init and waits for the next CM_SLAC_PARM.REQ instead of entering FailedState; only the second failure is terminal (matching.cpp L166-180). THE KEY STRUCTURAL FINDING FOR YOUR RULE

The division of labour between the two specs is clean, and it matters for how you cite:
- HomePlug GP defines the MME names, the MMTYPE numbers, the frame layouts, and the wire encoding of the negotiated fields (NUM_SOUNDS, and TIME_OUT expressed as N x 100 ms). Wireshark labels these "HOMEPLUG_AV_GP_MMTYPE_*". Values are stable and cross-verified across four independent codebases.
- ISO 15118-3 supplies the matching *procedure* timing and counts (the TT_*, TP_*, C_* symbols), pins the negotiated HPGP fields to fixed values (NUM_SOUNDS = 10, TIME_OUT = 6 = 600 ms, RESP_TYPE = 0x01), and adds CM_VALIDATE. So: the MMTYPEs you should cite to HomePlug GP; the timing you must cite to ISO 15118-3. Do not attribute the TT_* symbols to HomePlug GP - I found no evidence HPGP defines them, and one direct piece of evidence that it does not.

WHAT THIS MEANS FOR YOUR 10 s THRESHOLD - THE IMPORTANT CAVEAT

Your current rule fires on a CM_SLAC_MATCH.REQ that goes unanswered for 10 s. There is no normative 10 s limit for that event. The normative budget for an unanswered request inside the matching sequence is TT_match_response = 200 ms with C_EV_match_retry = 2 retries, i.e. about 600 ms total, and TT_match_sequence = 400 ms caps the gap between consecutive sequence messages. A 10 s wait is already an order of magnitude past failure; your detector is not firing early, it is firing very late.

There are two different 10 s constants in the standard, and it would be easy but wrong to grab either as the citation:
- TT_EVSE_match_session = 10 s is the EVSE waiting FOR CM_SLAC_MATCH.REQ (or CM_VALIDATE.REQ). Opposite direction from your rule, and anchored to the end of TT_EVSE_match_MNBC, not to the request.
- TT_matching_repetition = 10 s is the total window for repeated whole-sequence attempts, not for one request.

My recommendation: cite TT_match_response (200 ms) and C_EV_match_retry (2) as the normative basis for "an unanswered CM_SLAC_MATCH.REQ means matching has failed", and if you want to keep a conservative 10 s wall-clock so the rule stays quiet on slow-but-recovering sessions, cite the DOE/ChargeX rationale for it explicitly as an operational deviation - "Matching processing is likely to fail if it has not matched after 10 s" (NREL/INL, DOE/GO-102025-6649, Table 2 footnote a) - rather than dressing the 10 s up as a spec limit. That keeps the two kinds of evidence separate, which is what the ISO 15118-2 rules already do.

Also worth adding as cheap, well-grounded companion rules, since each has a hard normative number and is directly reconstructable from what your detector already parses: CM_ATTEN_CHAR.IND later than TT_EV_atten_results = 1200 ms after the first CM_START_ATTEN_CHAR.IND; sound burst not complete within TT_EVSE_match_MNBC = 600 ms; fewer than C_EV_start_atten_char_inds = 3 START_ATTEN_CHAR.IND or fewer than C_EV_match_MNBC = 10 MNBC_SOUND.IND; and no logical link within TT_match_join = 12 s after CM_SLAC_MATCH.CNF.

BOTTOM LINE FOR THE DETECTOR RULE

Your current rule ("match request unanswered for 10 s") is almost certainly citing the wrong direction of the protocol if you attach it to a 10 s symbol. Two distinct normative timers are in play:

1. EV waits for CM_SLAC_MATCH.CNF after sending CM_SLAC_MATCH.REQ -> governed by TT_match_response = 200 ms, with the whole run retried C_EV_match_retry = 2 times, and consecutive messages of the matching sequence bounded by TT_match_sequence = 400 ms. This is the timer an "unanswered match request" violates. A 10 s gap is ~50x over the normative limit.

2. EVSE waits for CM_SLAC_MATCH.REQ (or CM_VALIDATE.REQ) after it sent CM_ATTEN_CHAR.RSP -> governed by TT_EVSE_match_session = 10 s.

The coincidence is worth flagging: the fleet-measured 10 s threshold is exactly TT_EVSE_match_session. If your detector is timing from the EVSE's last message rather than from the EV's CM_SLAC_MATCH.REQ, the 10 s you measured may literally be chargers giving up on their own match-session timer, not an arbitrary empirical threshold. Recommend checking which endpoint's frame starts your clock before choosing the symbol to cite. If it starts at the EV's CM_SLAC_MATCH.REQ, cite TT_match_response (200 ms) + C_EV_match_retry (2); if it starts at the EVSE's CM_ATTEN_CHAR.RSP, cite TT_EVSE_match_session (10 s).

RETRY AND FAILURE BEHAVIOUR

- Whole-run retry: C_EV_match_retry = 2 (libslac, Rust crate). pyslac instead reads the limit as C_conn_max_match = min 3 and openly admits it could not find the ISO requirement for it. These two are in tension; do not treat the retry count as settled. C_EV_match_retry = 2 has two independent implementations behind it, C_conn_max_match = 3 has one that flags its own uncertainty.
- Retry pacing: TT_matching_rate = 400 ms between attempts ([V2G3-A09-124]).
- Overall retry window: TT_matching_repetition = 10 s ([V2G3-A09-125]); when it expires the matching process is FAILED and the state machine stops in "Unmatched" (Figure 11 of the standard). Note this is a second, different 10 s constant — do not confuse it with TT_EVSE_match_session.
- AC-specific reset path ([V2G3-M06-07]): if an AC EVSE at 5% CP duty cycle gets no SLAC request within TT_EVSE_SLAC_init, it goes to CP state E or F for at least T_step_EF (4 s), returns to 5%, and resets TT_EVSE_SLAC_init. This produces a repeating ~TT_EVSE_SLAC_init + 4 s cycle in captures that looks like repeated SLAC restarts — worth encoding as a distinct signature rather than as a fault.
- Plug-out handling ([V2G3-A09-121], cited in pyslac issue #15): the low-layer comms module shall leave the logical network, reset the NMK, and switch matching state to "Unmatched".

WHAT ANSWERS YOUR ACTUAL RULE (unanswered CM_SLAC_MATCH.REQ)
The current fleet threshold of 10 s does not map to a single normative symbol; the normative chain is much tighter and has three layers:
1. Per-message: the EV waits TT_match_response = 200 ms for CM_SLAC_MATCH.CNF after CM_SLAC_MATCH.REQ. Expected (performance) latency is TP_match_response = 100 ms.
2. Per-attempt: on timeout the EV retries, bounded by C_EV_match_retry = 2, i.e. at most 3 transmissions, so a matching attempt dies after roughly 3 x 200 ms = 600 ms of silence. EVerest implements exactly this: lib/everest/slac/fsm/ev/src/states/others.cpp, MatchRequestState::callback() lines 147-169 (`if (num_of_tries < slac::defs::C_EV_MATCH_RETRY) return send_match_req();` else `return Event::FAILED;`) with `next_timeout = now + TT_MATCH_RESPONSE_MS` set in send_match_req() at line 210.
3. Per-session: a failed attempt waits TT_matching_rate = 400 ms, and repetitions are allowed only within TT_matching_repetition = 10 s, with at most C_conn_max_match = 3 matching processes. Independently, the EVSE gives up waiting for CM_SLAC_MATCH.REQ at TT_EVSE_match_session = 10 s after TT_EVSE_match_MNBC expires.
So your measured 10 s coincides with TWO different 10 s normative symbols (TT_matching_repetition and TT_EVSE_match_session). If the rule is "EV sent CM_SLAC_MATCH.REQ, no CM_SLAC_MATCH.CNF within 10 s", the symbol to cite is TT_matching_repetition (the whole matching window), and you could add a much more sensitive second rule at TT_match_response = 200 ms with C_EV_match_retry = 2 that fires roughly 600 ms in. Be careful which side you are asserting about: TT_EVSE_match_session is the EVSE's deadline for the REQ to ARRIVE, not for the CNF to come back.

Also worth wiring in: if CM_SLAC_MATCH.CNF is seen but the AVLN never forms, the symbol is TT_match_join = 12 s (max). That is a distinct failure mode from an unanswered REQ and is probably already visible in your captures as a matched-but-no-traffic case.

=== 8. WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE DETECTOR RULE, AND WHAT IS STILL MISSING ===
  - The fleet-measured 10 s threshold for an unanswered CM_SLAC_MATCH.REQ cannot be replaced with a normative symbol from anything in the public domain. The value is in ISO 15118-3:2015 Annex A, Table A.1, p. 30–71 range, and nowhere else that is free.
  - Once a copy is purchased, the efficient path is: open Table A.1 first, then Figure A.9 (matching-process error handling) and subclause 9.7 (Error handling, p. 27) for the retry/abort semantics, then §5.2's [V2G3-Axx-yyy] code for the requirement ID the rule should quote. Total reading: well under 10 pages.
  - Secondary confirmation, if the budget stretches: ISO 15118-5:2018 Table 29 (pp. 28–45) to name the exact requirement ID, and Annex A.1 (p. 164) for the corresponding test timer.
  - Open question I could not settle from free sources: whether the normative limit is expressed as a single response timeout (TT_match_response) plus a retry count (C_EV_match_retry) whose product is the effective give-up time, or as an overall sequence budget (TT_match_sequence). That distinction decides whether our 10 s rule should fire on one unanswered request or on an exhausted retry series, and it is answerable only from Table A.1 plus Figure A.9.

===============================================================
1. ORDERED MESSAGE EXCHANGE (who sends what)
===============================================================
Pre-conditions. EVSE: control-pilot transition A/E/F -> Bx/Cx/Dx arms TT_EVSE_SLAC_init and puts the EVSE into "Matching". EV: TP_EV_SLAC_init (10 s) bounds plug-in -> first request. Before any of this the EVSE's own modem is keyed: EVerest sends CM_SET_KEY.REQ to its local modem in the Reset state, i.e. BEFORE matching, generating a fresh NMK per session.

 1. EV -> broadcast  CM_SLAC_PARM.REQ        (EV picks the 8-byte RunID; Ioniq uses its MAC + 0x0000, Tesla uses the ASCII "TESLA EV")
 2. EVSE -> EV       CM_SLAC_PARM.CNF        (carries NUM_SOUNDS = 10 and TIMEOUT = 0x06 = 600 ms = TT_EVSE_match_MNBC)
 3. EV -> broadcast  CM_START_ATTEN_CHAR.IND x3   (C_EV_start_atten_char_inds; spaced TP_EV_batch_msg_interval 20-50 ms; the PLC chip forwards only one to the application)
 4. EV -> broadcast  CM_MNBC_SOUND.IND x10        (C_EV_match_MNBC; spaced 20-50 ms; the "remaining sound count" field decrements [V2G3-A09-28/-29])
 5. EVSE modem -> EVSE HLE  CM_ATTEN_PROFILE.IND  (one per sound; local to the EVSE, will only appear in a capture taken on the EVSE's own PLC interface)
 6. EVSE averages the 58 attenuation groups once all sounds are in OR TT_EVSE_match_MNBC expires [V2G3-A09-19], within TP_EVSE_avg_atten_calc (100 ms)
 7. EVSE -> EV       CM_ATTEN_CHAR.IND       (58 groups, num_sounds actually captured)
 8. EV picks its EVSE (thresholds C_EV_match_signalattn_direct = 10, _indirect = 20) and replies to that one only:
    EV -> EVSE       CM_ATTEN_CHAR.RSP       (result must be 0x00)
 9. OPTIONAL  EV <-> EVSE  CM_VALIDATE.REQ/.CNF (BCB-toggle validation). Almost never seen; EVerest logs "Received CM_VALIDATE.REQ / not implemented - will return failure code"; pyslac does not implement it.
10. EV -> EVSE       CM_SLAC_MATCH.REQ
11. EVSE -> EV       CM_SLAC_MATCH.CNF       (carries NID (7 B) + NMK (16 B) - this is the payload the EV needs)
12. EV -> its own modem  CM_SET_KEY.REQ / .CNF  (PID = 0x04 "HLE protocol" per ISO 15118-3); the modem resets, then both modems join the same AVLN
13. Link comes up -> AMP MAP window (TT_amp_map_exchange 200 ms; if no CM_AMP_MAP.REQ, assume none) -> D-LINK_READY.indication to the HLE -> matching state "Matched"
14. ONLY THEN V2G: EVCC sends the SDP request (UDP multicast, ISO 15118-2), gets the SDP response with the SECC's link-local IPv6 address and port, opens TCP (or TLS), and sends SupportedAppProtocolReq.

Detector-relevant asymmetry: CM_SET_KEY frames are HomePlug MMEs on the same EtherType 0x88E1 but are addressed to the LOCAL modem, not to the peer. A capture on one side normally shows only that side's SET_KEY. Absence of the EV's CM_SET_KEY in an EVSE-side capture is expected, not a fault.

===============================================================
2. EVSE-SIDE TIMEOUT MAP (which timer guards which step)
===============================================================
From EVerest everest-core lib/everest/slac/fsm/evse/ (matching.cpp, matching_handle_slac.cpp) - the most explicit public mapping I found:

  enter Matching            -> arm slac_init_timeout_ms (TT_EVSE_SLAC_init)
                               expiry: "CM_SLAC_PARM_REQ timed out -> FAILED"
  after CM_SLAC_PARM.CNF    -> arm TT_MATCH_SEQUENCE_MS (400 ms) for CM_START_ATTEN_CHAR.IND
                               expiry: session -> FAILED
  after START_ATTEN_CHAR    -> arm TT_EVSE_MATCH_MNBC_MS (600 ms) sounding window
                               expiry: NOT a failure; sub-state -> FINALIZE_SOUNDING (+45 ms) and average anyway
  send CM_ATTEN_CHAR.IND    -> arm TT_MATCH_RESPONSE_MS (200 ms) for CM_ATTEN_CHAR.RSP
                               expiry: retry (re-send atten char) while num_retries <= C_EV_MATCH_RETRY (2), else FAILED
  after CM_ATTEN_CHAR.RSP   -> arm TT_EVSE_MATCH_SESSION_MS (10 000 ms) for CM_VALIDATE.REQ / CM_SLAC_MATCH.REQ
                               expiry: "Waiting for CM_SLAC_MATCH_REQ timed out -> failed"
  after CM_SLAC_MATCH.CNF   -> optional WaitForLinkState, polls vendor LINK_STATUS every 100 ms up to
                               link_status_timeout_ms (10 s default; the normative figure is TT_match_join = 12 s)
                               expiry: Event::RETRY_MATCHING
  MatchedState::enter()     -> signal_dlink_ready(true): this is the exact moment the higher layer is told it may start V2G.

Reference-point ambiguity worth writing into the rule: Table A.1 (guru transcription) defines TT_EVSE_match_session as running "from the expiration of TT_EVSE_match_MNBC"; pyslac's comment says "after reception of CM_ATTEN_CHAR.RSP"; EVerest arms it on CM_ATTEN_CHAR.RSP and carries an explicit FIXME - "referring to the standard, it is not clear here, if we should offset from TT_EVSE_MATCH_MNBC". The difference is the sounding window plus the EV's think-time, ~0.6-1.6 s in practice.

===============================================================
3. EV-SIDE RETRY BEHAVIOUR
===============================================================
Per-message retries (EVerest lib/everest/slac/fsm/ev/src/states/others.cpp):
 - CM_SLAC_PARM.REQ: arm TT_match_response (200 ms), resend on expiry. EVerest deliberately uses `num_of_tries < 100` with the comment "the norm says num_of_tries < slac::defs::C_EV_MATCH_RETRY but doesn't seem to work in 'real life'". So long bursts of repeated CM_SLAC_PARM.REQ in a capture are normal field behaviour.
 - CM_SLAC_MATCH.REQ: arm TT_match_response (200 ms), resend while `num_of_tries < C_EV_MATCH_RETRY` (2), then Event::FAILED. Total ~600 ms from first REQ to give-up.
 - Sounding: TT_EV_atten_results (1200 ms) runs from the FIRST CM_START_ATTEN_CHAR.IND; if it expires with no usable CM_ATTEN_CHAR.IND the attempt fails [V2G3-A09-30/-31/-32]. The guru EV model wires this as CollectConfirmations -> NoPotentialEVSEFound -> SLACFailed.
EVSE-side duplicate handling: EVerest's WaitForLinkState explicitly re-sends CM_SLAC_MATCH.CNF when it sees a repeated CM_SLAC_MATCH.REQ ("Received CM_SLAC_MATCH.REQ retry from EV, sending out CM_SLAC_MATCH.CNF again."). A duplicate REQ therefore does not imply a fault.
Malformed/mismatched frames are IGNORED, not fatal: pyslac cites [V2G3-A09-47] for CM_ATTEN_CHAR.RSP with the wrong RunID/EtherType and [V2G3-A09-98] for CM_SLAC_MATCH.REQ with the wrong RunID ("it shall be ignored"). EVerest logs "Invalid ... received, ignoring" / "No session found for ...".

===============================================================
4. WHOLE-SEQUENCE RETRIES AND TERMINAL FAILURE
===============================================================
Inner loop (SLAC level):
 - A failed matching attempt -> wait TT_matching_rate (400 ms) before restarting [V2G3-A09-124].
 - Restarts are bounded BOTH by a count, C_conn_max_match = 3 (minimum), AND by a window, TT_matching_repetition = 10 s. When either is exhausted the matching process stops in "Unmatched" state [V2G3-A09-125]. pyslac notes candidly that it could not find an explicit ISO requirement for the count-exhaustion case but that the behaviour is the same.
 - The guru EV model encodes this as: TT_matching_repetition started once at doStartSLAC; transitions ParameterExchange -> SLACFailedTotally and SignalStrengthMeasurement -> SLACFailedTotally both fire on evTT_matching_repetition_timeout.

Outer loop (control-pilot level, AC):
 - [V2G3-M06-07]: if an AC EVSE at 5% duty cycle receives NO SLAC request within TT_EVSE_SLAC_init, it shall go to CP state E or F for T_step_EF (min 4 s), return to 5% duty cycle, and reset TT_EVSE_SLAC_init before being ready to answer a matching request again. Retried C_sequ_retry = 2 times. "At the end, without any reaction, the EVSE shall go to state X1." (verbatim from pyslac enums.py lines 18-24.)
 - Vendor confirmation of the terminal state: INSYS Powerline GP raises HC_STATUS.IND = 0x00 Timeout_TT_EVSE_SLAC_init meaning "no SLAC association could be achieved. It will not respond on any SLAC requests following this timeout."

Teardown / unmatch:
 - [V2G3-M09-17] and section A.9.7: on leaving the logical network the session parameters are reset to defaults, the NMK is reset, and the state becomes "Unmatched". TP_match_leave = 1 s bounds the leave. pyslac issue #15 flags that failing to reset the NMK is a real compliance gap ([V2G3-A09-121]) because the EV may then not detect the absence of an existing logical network on the next plug-in.
 - EVerest has a non-normative `reset_instead_of_fail` option that re-arms MatchingState once (clears sessions, re-arms TT_EVSE_SLAC_init) instead of going to FailedState.

Vendor-exposed failure taxonomy (INSYS Powerline GP, HC_STATUS.IND byte 18) maps 1:1 onto the ISO timers and is a good template for detector labels:
  0x00 Timeout_TT_EVSE_SLAC_init       - no SLAC association achieved; stops answering SLAC
  0x02 Timeout_TT_EVSE_match_MNBC
  0x03 Timeout_TT_EVSE_match_session   - "has sent an attenuation profile to a PEV, but not received a response from this"
  0x04 Timeout_TT_match_join           - "an association has been executed between PEV and EVSE, but an AVLN could not be established"
  0x05 Timeout_TT_match_sequence
  0x06 Timeout_TT_match_response
  0x07 System_init_Failed

===============================================================
5. WHAT MUST HAPPEN BEFORE THE V2G TCP SESSION CAN START
===============================================================
Ordered preconditions:
 (a) CM_SLAC_MATCH.CNF delivered with NID + NMK.
 (b) EV applies them via CM_SET_KEY.REQ to its own modem; modem resets/re-associates.
 (c) Both modems join the same AVLN and the PLC link comes up. Bounded by TT_match_join = 12 s from CM_SLAC_MATCH.CNF; on expiry the EV retries the matching process and the EVSE resets its state machine.
 (d) AMP MAP window: TT_amp_map_exchange = 200 ms after link detection; if no CM_AMP_MAP.REQ arrives, no AMP MAP exchange takes place and D-LINK_READY.indication goes to the HLE (performance timer TP_link_ready_notification = 1 s).
 (e) State = "Matched" / D-LINK_READY(link established). EVerest expresses this as `ctx.signal_dlink_ready(true)` on MatchedState::enter(); INSYS as D_LINK_READY.IND result 0x00. Only now is HLC allowed.
 (f) SDP (ISO 15118-2): EVCC sends the SDP request over UDP multicast; expects the SDP response within 250 ms; up to 50 requests total, then falls back to basic PWM charging.
 (g) TCP (or TLS) connect to the address/port from the SDP response, then SupportedAppProtocolReq -> SessionSetupReq.
 (h) Outer -2 budget: V2G_EVCC_CommunicationSetup_Performance_Time = 20 s covers SDP + SupportedAppProtocol + SessionSetup.

Expected CM_SLAC_MATCH.CNF -> first V2G message:
 - There is NO normative lower or upper bound on this gap beyond TT_match_join = 12 s (which bounds MATCH.CNF -> link up, not MATCH.CNF -> SDP). I could not find a public source giving a tighter normative number, and I would rather report that than invent one.
 - Best empirical figure: 4.1 s, measured off a production Hyundai Ioniq and recorded as the reference behaviour in pyPLC (pyPlcHomeplug.py line 1152).
 - Qualcomm's reference PEV sleeps SLAC_SETTLETIME = 10 s after CM_SET_KEY before treating the link as usable; pyslac copies this as SLAC_SETTLE_TIME = 10. Stacks derived from open-plc-utils will therefore show a much larger gap.
 - Practical detector guidance: expect roughly 1-10 s; do not raise a fault below 12 s (TT_match_join) unless the link-up itself is observable as failed.

===============================================================
6. MAPPING TO THE EXISTING RULE (10 s unanswered match request)
===============================================================
Two different normative symbols could back a "match request unanswered" rule, and they are ~50x apart. Which one to cite depends on exactly which edge the detector reconstructs:

 (A) Edge = "EV sent CM_SLAC_MATCH.REQ and no CM_SLAC_MATCH.CNF was observed."
     Normative limit: TT_match_response = 200 ms, with the EV allowed C_EV_match_retry = 2 resends -> the whole thing is normatively over in about 600 ms. A 10 s threshold is ~17x looser than the norm and will miss genuinely slow-but-eventually-answered EVSEs that the standard already considers failed.

 (B) Edge = "EVSE sent CM_ATTEN_CHAR.IND / received CM_ATTEN_CHAR.RSP and never saw a CM_SLAC_MATCH.REQ."
     Normative limit: TT_EVSE_match_session = 10 s exactly. This is almost certainly what the fleet measurement rediscovered. Independent corroboration of the semantics from a PLC modem vendor: INSYS Powerline GP raises Timeout_TT_EVSE_match_session for precisely "has sent an attenuation profile to a PEV, but not received a response from this."

If the rule is (B), it can now cite TT_EVSE_match_session = 10 s, ISO 15118-3 Table A.1, exactly the way the ISO 15118-2 rules cite their symbols - with the documented caveat that sources disagree on whether the timer starts at TT_EVSE_match_MNBC expiry or at CM_ATTEN_CHAR.RSP reception (EVerest flags this ambiguity in code).

Do NOT build the rule on TP_EV_match_session = 500 ms ("performance timer for the EV to start validation or SLAC_MATCH after sending CM_ATTEN_CHAR.RSP"). The TP_* family are performance timers, not hard timeouts, and a real Ioniq measures 860-980 ms on exactly that edge - a TP_EV_match_session rule would false-positive on a compliant, healthy EV.

Other pcap-observable normative edges worth adding while the symbols are being wired in:
  CM_SLAC_PARM.REQ  -> CM_SLAC_PARM.CNF        : TT_match_response 200 ms (x C_EV_match_retry 2)
  CM_SLAC_PARM.CNF  -> CM_START_ATTEN_CHAR.IND : TT_match_sequence 400 ms (EVSE-side wait)
  1st START_ATTEN_CHAR.IND -> CM_ATTEN_CHAR.IND: TT_EV_atten_results 1200 ms (EV-side wait)
  last MNBC_SOUND   -> CM_ATTEN_CHAR.IND       : TT_EVSE_match_MNBC 600 ms + TP_EVSE_avg_atten_calc 100 ms
  CM_ATTEN_CHAR.IND -> CM_ATTEN_CHAR.RSP       : TT_match_response 200 ms (x C_EV_match_retry 2)
  CM_ATTEN_CHAR.RSP -> CM_SLAC_MATCH.REQ       : TT_EVSE_match_session 10 s
  CM_SLAC_MATCH.REQ -> CM_SLAC_MATCH.CNF       : TT_match_response 200 ms (x C_EV_match_retry 2)
  CM_SLAC_MATCH.CNF -> link up / D-LINK_READY  : TT_match_join 12 s
  CP B detected     -> CM_SLAC_PARM.REQ        : TT_EVSE_SLAC_init 20-50 s (EVSE), TP_EV_SLAC_init 10 s (EV)
  count checks      : exactly 3 CM_START_ATTEN_CHAR.IND, exactly 10 CM_MNBC_SOUND.IND, 58 AAG groups, sound spacing 20-50 ms
  whole-sequence    : restarts spaced TT_matching_rate 400 ms, bounded by C_conn_max_match 3 and TT_matching_repetition 10 s
